title: Andon Deck for Claude Code – your Stream Deck as an andon board
description: See what Claude Code is doing from across the room. Approve tool calls, queue prompts and watch plan limits on your Stream Deck. Free, local, open source.
kicker: a Stream Deck plugin for Claude Code
h1: Claude Code, readable from across the room.
lead: Andon Deck turns your Stream Deck into an andon board for Claude Code. Every key's border shows what Claude is doing – working, waiting for you, or stopped – so you can look away while it works. Approve tool calls from the deck, queue the next prompt, keep an eye on your plan limits. Free, local, open source.
works: for Stream Deck · Mini · XL · + · + XL · Neo · Studio · Pedal · Mobile · Virtual · Galleon 100 SD – Windows and macOS, Claude Code in WSL too
demoAria: Animated Stream Deck XL running Andon Deck through a Claude Code turn
s1: Claude is idle. The session key sleeps; the rest of the deck is ready.
s2: You send a prompt. A light runs the border while Claude works.
s3: Queue the next prompt now – it waits until this turn ends.
s4: Claude wants to run a command. Allow, Always and Deny light up with what it is.
s5: On any other profile, the whole deck calls you – any key brings you back.
s6: Allow. Claude carries on, no window switching.
s7: Turn done – your queued prompt starts on its own.
s8: And the 5-hour limit warns before you run out, not after.
quote: On a factory floor, one light tells the whole hall what a machine needs. Your Stream Deck can do that for Claude.
manifesto: Claude Code works for minutes at a time, then needs you for a second: a permission, a question, a finished turn. Andon Deck makes that second impossible to miss and quick to answer – the state lives on every key's border, readable out of the corner of your eye, and the answer is one press away.
edgeLead: Colour is reserved for machine state. Keys you press are graphite, so a lit key always means Claude is telling you something.
f1Text: Allow, Always allow or Deny the request Claude Code is waiting on. The key shows the tool and the command – and exactly what an Always would store.
f2Text: Line up “run the tests” or “commit” while Claude works; it starts the moment the turn ends. A clipboard key sends whatever you just copied, an error message for example.
f3Text: Stop denies every further tool call, so Claude winds down and reports back. Autopilot approves read-only tools – or all of them – for a set time, counting down on the key.
f4Text: The 5-hour and weekly limits, live from Claude Code. If the current pace runs out before the reset, the key says when: full in 1h 20m.
f4Alt: Dial readout: 5-hour limit at 78 %, full in 1 h 20 min, with the curve so far
f5Text: Tokens by hour and by day, read straight from Claude Code's transcripts – a full week of history from the first minute. On a dial, the curves draw themselves.
f5Alt: Dial readout: tokens per day over the last week
f6Text: Up to four session keys, each with Clawd posed for its state, plus context pressure, the model in use and a turn timer. Pin one and every other key follows it.
alertTitle: when Claude needs you, the whole deck says so
alertText: On a permission request or a question, every connected deck switches to a full-screen Clawd waving across all its keys – whatever profile it was showing, OBS or Spotify included.
alertFact1: any key takes you back to where you were
alertFact2: answered in the terminal? it steps aside by itself
alertFact3: a finished turn does not raise it – only real questions
alertAria: Animated Stream Deck XL showing one large waving Clawd across all keys
devLead: Ready-made profiles for every Stream Deck with keys, each built for its grid rather than cropped from a bigger one. Hold the Connect key to switch to yours.
i1Text: Double-click the downloaded .streamDeckPlugin. Stream Deck installs it with its profiles.
i2Text: The Connect key writes Claude Code's hooks for you – on Windows, macOS, or with Claude Code inside WSL. Your own hooks and status line stay as they are.
i3Text: Start Claude Code as usual. The deck follows every session on its own; nothing to configure per project.
p1: Nothing leaves your machine. The deck talks to Claude Code over a local port. No server, no account, no telemetry.
p2: Your settings stay yours. Hooks are added next to your own and removed cleanly; an existing status line keeps running.
p3: Read, never uploaded. Usage history comes from transcripts on your disk and stays there.
p4: Open source, MIT. Every line is on GitHub to read, fork and improve.
footer: Andon Deck · MIT · open source, no tracking, no cookies
